1.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh in the Wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Appointment, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they had come out of the land of Mitsrayim, saying,
1.2: “Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl, by their clans, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of names, every male, head by head,
1.3: from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army in Yisra’ĕl. Number them by their divisions, you and Aharon.
1.4: “And a man from every tribe should be with you, each one the head of his father’s house.
1.5: “And these are the names of the men who stand with you. From Re’uḇĕn: Elitsur, son of Sheḏĕy’ur.
1.10: “From the sons of Yosĕph: From Ephrayim: Elishama, son of Ammihuḏ. From Menashsheh: Gamli’ĕl, son of Peḏahtsur.
1.16: These are the ones called from the congregation, leaders of their fathers’ tribes, heads of the thousands of Yisra’ĕl.
1.17: And Mosheh and Aharon took these men who were called by name,
1.18: and they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month. And they declared their ancestry by clans, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, each one head by head.
1.19: As 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh, so he registered them in the Wilderness of Sinai.
1.20: And the children of Re’uḇĕn, Yisra’ĕl’s first-born, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, every male head by head, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.21: those who were registered of the tribe of Re’uḇĕn were forty-six thousand five hundred.
1.22: From the children of Shim’on, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, of those who were registered, according to the number of names, every male head by head, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.23: those who were registered of the tribe of Shim’on were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
1.24: From the children of Gaḏ, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.25: those who were registered of the tribe of Gaḏ were forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
1.26: From the children of Yahuḏah, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.27: those who were registered of the tribe of Yahuḏah were seventy-four thousand six hundred.
1.28: From the children of Yissasḵar, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.29: those who were registered of the tribe of Yissasḵar were fifty-four thousand four hundred.
1.30: From the children of Zeḇulun, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.31: those who were registered of the tribe of Zeḇulun were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
1.32: From the sons of Yosĕph, the children of Ephrayim, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.33: those who were registered of the tribe of Ephrayim were forty thousand five hundred.
1.34: From the children of Menashsheh, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.35: those who were registered of the tribe of Menashsheh were thirty-two thousand two hundred.
1.36: From the children of Binyamin, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.37: those who were registered of the tribe of Binyamin were thirty-five thousand four hundred.
1.38: From the children of Dan, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.39: those who were registered of the tribe of Dan were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
1.40: From the children of Ashĕr, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.41: those who were registered of the tribe of Ashĕr were forty-one thousand five hundred.
1.42: From the children of Naphtali, their genealogies by their clans, by their fathers’ house, according to the number of names, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army,
1.43: those who were registered of the tribe of Naphtali were fifty-three thousand four hundred.
1.44: These were those registered, whom Mosheh and Aharon registered, with the leaders of Yisra’ĕl, twelve men, each one for his father’s house.
1.45: And all those that were registered of the children of Yisra’ĕl, by their fathers’ houses, from twenty years old and above, everyone going out to the army in Yisra’ĕl,
1.46: all those that were registered were six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
1.47: But the Lĕwites were not registered among them by their fathers’ tribe,
1.48: because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had spoken to Mosheh, saying,
1.49: “Only the tribe of Lĕwi you do not register, nor take a census of them among the children of Yisra’ĕl.
1.50: “Instead, appoint the Lĕwites over the Mishkan of the Witness, over all its furnishings, and over all that belongs to it. They bear the Mishkan and all its furnishings, and they attend to it, and camp around the Mishkan.
1.51: “And when the Mishkan is to go forward, the Lĕwites take it down. And when the Mishkan is to be put up, the Lĕwites put it up. And the stranger who comes near is put to death.
1.52: “And the children of Yisra’ĕl shall pitch their tents, everyone by his own camp, everyone by his own banner, according to their divisions,
1.53: but let the Lĕwites camp around the Mishkan of the Witness, so that there be no wrath on the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl. And the Lĕwites shall guard the duty of the Mishkan of the Witness.”
1.54: And the children of Yisra’ĕl did according to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh, so they did.

10.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
10.2: “Make two silver trumpets for yourself, make them of beaten work. And you shall use them for calling the congregation and for breaking camp.
10.3: “And when they blow both of them, all the congregation shall meet before you at the door of the Tent of Appointment.
10.4: “And if they blow one, then the leaders, the heads of the thousands of Yisra’ĕl, shall gather to you.
10.5: “And when you blow a shout, the camps that lie on the east side shall depart.
10.6: “And when you blow a shout the second time, then the camps that lie on the south side shall depart - they blow a shout for them to depart.
10.7: “And when the assembly is to be assembled, you blow, but do not shout.
10.8: “And the sons of Aharon, the kohenim, blow with the trumpets. And it shall be to you for a Law forever throughout your generations.
10.9: “And when you go into battle in your land against the enemy that distresses you, then you shall shout with the trumpets, and you shall be remembered before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, and you shall be saved from your enemies.
10.10: “And in the day of your gladness, and in your Appointed Times, and at the beginning of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your peace offerings. And they shall be a remembrance for you before your Elohim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.”
10.11: And it came to be on the twentieth day of the second month, in the second year, that the cloud was taken up from above the Mishkan of the Witness.
10.12: And the children of Yisra’ĕl departed, journeying from the Wilderness of Sinai. And the cloud dwelt in the Wilderness of Paran.
10.13: Thus they departed the first time, according to the command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 by the hand of Mosheh.
10.14: And the banner of the camp of the children of Yahuḏah departed first according to their divisions. And over their army was Naḥshon, son of Amminaḏaḇ.
10.15: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Yissasḵar was Nethan’ĕl, son of Tsu’ar.
10.16: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Zeḇulun was Eliyaḇ, son of Ḥĕlon.
10.17: And the Mishkan was taken down. And the sons of Gĕreshon and the sons of Merari departed, bearing the Mishkan.
10.18: And the banner of the camp of Re’uḇĕn departed according to their divisions. And over their army was Elitsur, son of Sheḏĕy’ur.
10.19: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Shim’on was Shelumi’ĕl, son of Tsurishaddai.
10.20: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Gaḏ was Elyasaph, the son of Deu’ĕl.
10.21: And the Qehathites departed, bearing the Miqdash, while the Mishkan was put up before they came.
10.22: And the banner of the camp of the children of Ephrayim departed according to their divisions. And over their army was Elishama, son of Ammihuḏ.
10.23: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Menashsheh was Gamli’ĕl, son of Peḏahtsur.
10.24: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Binyamin was Aḇiḏan, son of Giḏ’oni.
10.25: Then the banner of the camp of the children of Dan, which formed the rear guard of all the camps, departed according to their divisions. And over their army was Aḥi’ezer, son of Ammishaddai.
10.26: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Ashĕr was Paḡ’i’ĕl, the son of Oḵran.
10.27: And over the army of the tribe of the children of Naphtali was Aḥira, the son of Ĕynan.
10.28: Such was the order of departure of the children of Yisra’ĕl, according to their divisions, when they departed.
10.29: And Mosheh said to Ḥoḇaḇ, the son of Re’uw’ĕl the Miḏyanite, Mosheh’s father-in-law, “We are departing for the place of which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, ‘I give it to you.’ Come with us, and we shall do good to you, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken good concerning Yisra’ĕl.”
10.30: And he replied to him, “I am not going, but I am going to my own land and to my relatives.”
10.31: Then he said, “Please do not leave us, because you know how we are to camp in the wilderness, and you shall be our eyes.
10.32: “And it shall be, when you go with us, then it shall be that whatever good 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 does to us, the same we shall do to you.”
10.33: So they departed from the mountain of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 on a journey of three days. And the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 went before them for the three days’ journey, to seek out a resting place for them.
10.34: And the cloud of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was above them by day when they went out from the camp.
10.35: And it came to be, whenever the ark departed, that Mosheh said, “Rise up, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄! And let Your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate You flee before You.”
10.36: And when it rested, he said, “Return, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to the countless thousands of Yisra’ĕl.”

11.1: And it came to be, when the people were as complainers, it was evil in the ears of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 heard it, and His displeasure burned. And the fire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned among them, and consumed those in the outskirts of the camp.
11.2: And the people cried out to Mosheh, and Mosheh prayed to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and the fire died down.
11.3: Then he called the name of the place Taḇ’ĕrah, because the fire of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had burned among them.
11.4: And the mixed multitude who were in their midst lusted greatly, so the children of Yisra’ĕl also wept again and said, “Who is giving us meat to eat?
11.5: “We remember the fish which we ate without cost in Mitsrayim, the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic,
11.6: but now our life is dried up. There is naught to look at but this manna!”
11.7: Now the manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium.
11.8: The people went about and gathered it, ground it on millstones or beat it in the mortar, and cooked it in a pot, and made cakes of it. And its taste was as the taste of cakes baked with oil.
11.9: And when the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell on it.
11.10: And Mosheh heard the people weeping throughout their clans, each man at the door of his tent. And the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned exceedingly. And in the eyes of Mosheh it was evil,
11.11: so Mosheh said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Why have You done evil to Your servant? And why have I not found favor in Your eyes, to put the burden of all these people on me?
11.12: “Was it I who conceived all these people? Was it I who brought them forth, that You should say to me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as the foster father carries a nursing child,’ to the land which You swore to their fathers?
11.13: “Where am I to get meat to give to all these people? For they weep before me, saying, ‘Give us meat to eat.’
11.14: “I am unable to bear all these people alone, because the burden is too heavy for me.
11.15: “And if You are doing this to me, please slay me altogether, if I have found favor in Your eyes, and let me not see my evil!”
11.16: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “Gather to Me seventy men of the elders of Yisra’ĕl, whom you know to be the elders of the people and officers over them. And bring them to the Tent of Appointment, and let them stand there with you.
11.17: “And I shall come down and speak with you there, and shall take of the Ruaḥ that is on you, and put on them. And they shall bear the burden of the people with you, so that you do not bear it yourself alone.
11.18: “And say to the people, ‘Qadosh yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat, because you have wept in the hearing of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, “Who is giving us meat to eat? For it was well with us in Mitsrayim.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall give you meat, and you shall eat.
11.19: ‘You are going to eat, not one day, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days,
11.20: but for a month of days, until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes an abomination to you, because you have rejected 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who is among you, and have wept before Him, saying, “Why did we come up out of Mitsrayim?” ’ ”
11.21: And Mosheh said, “The people in whose midst I am are six hundred thousand men on foot, and You, You have said, ‘I give them meat to eat for a month of days.’
11.22: “Could flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, to be sufficient for them? Or could all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to be sufficient for them?”
11.23: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “Is the arm of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 too short? Now see whether My word meets you or not!”
11.24: And Mosheh went out and spoke to the people the words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and he gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people and stood them around the Tent.
11.25: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the Ruaḥ that was upon him, and placed the same upon the seventy elders. And it came to be, when the Ruaḥ rested upon them, that they naḇu, but did not continue.
11.26: However, two men had remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldaḏ, and the name of the other Mĕyḏaḏ. And the Ruaḥ rested upon them. Now they were among those listed, but did not go out to the Tent. And they naḇu in the camp.
11.27: And a young man ran and informed Mosheh, and said, “Eldaḏ and Mĕyḏaḏ naḇa in the camp.”
11.28: And Yahoshua son of Nun, Mosheh’s assistant from his youth, answered and said, “Mosheh my master, forbid them!”
11.29: Then Mosheh said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Oh, that all the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 were neḇi’im, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 would put His Ruaḥ upon them!”
11.30: And Mosheh returned to the camp, both he and the elders of Yisra’ĕl.
11.31: And a wind went forth from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and it brought quail from the sea and let them fall beside the camp, about a day’s journey on this side and about a day’s journey on the other side, all around the camp, and about two ammah above the surface of the ground.
11.32: And the people were up all that day, and all that night, and all the next day, and gathered the quail. He who had least gathered ten ḥomers. And they spread them out for themselves all around the camp.
11.33: The meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, and the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned against the people, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 smote the people with an exceeding great plague.
11.34: Then he called the name of that place Qiḇroth ha’Tta’awah, because there they buried the people who had lusted.
11.35: From Qiḇroth ha’Tta’awah the people departed for Ḥatsĕroth - and they were at Ḥatsĕroth.

12.1: Now Miryam and Aharon spoke against Mosheh because of the Kushite wife whom he had taken, for he had taken a Kushite wife.
12.2: And they said, “Has 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoken only through Mosheh? Has He not also spoken through us?” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 heard it.
12.3: And the man Mosheh was very humble, more than all men who were on the face of the earth.
12.4: And suddenly 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, and Aharon, and Miryam, “You three, come out to the Tent of Appointment!” So the three came out.
12.5: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came down in the column of cloud and stood in the door of the Tent, and called Aharon and Miryam. And they both went forward.
12.6: And He said, “Hear now My words: If your naḇi is of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I make Myself known to him in a vision, and I speak to him in a dream.
12.7: “Not so with My servant Mosheh, he is trustworthy in all My house.
12.8: “I speak with him mouth to mouth, and plainly, and not in riddles. And he sees the form of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. So why were you not afraid to speak against My servant Mosheh?”
12.9: And the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned against them, and He left.
12.10: And the cloud turned away from above the Tent, and look: Miryam was leprous, as white as snow! And Aharon turned toward Miryam, and look: a leper!
12.11: And Aharon said to Mosheh, “Oh, my master! Please do not hold against us the sin in which we have done foolishly and in which we have sinned.
12.12: “Please do not let her be as one dead when coming out of its mother’s womb, with our flesh half consumed!”
12.13: And Mosheh cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, saying, “O Ĕl, please heal her, please!”
12.14: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “If her father had but spit in her face, would she not be ashamed seven days? Let her be shut out of the camp seven days, and after that let her be re-admitted.”
12.15: And Miryam was shut out of the camp seven days, and the people did not depart until Miryam was re-admitted.
12.16: And afterward the people departed from Ḥatsĕroth, and they camped in the Wilderness of Paran.

13.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
13.2: “Send men to spy out the land of Kena’an, which I am giving to the children of Yisra’ĕl. Send one man from each tribe of their fathers, every one a leader among them.”
13.3: And by the command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Mosheh sent them from the Wilderness of Paran, all of them men who were heads of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
13.4: And these were their names. From the tribe of Re’uḇĕn: Shammua, son of Zakkur.
13.5: From the tribe of Shim’on: Shaphat, son of Ḥori.
13.6: From the tribe of Yahuḏah: Kalĕḇ, son of Yephunneh.
13.7: From the tribe of Yissasḵar: Yiḡ’al, son of Yosĕph.
13.8: From the tribe of Ephrayim: Hoshĕa, son of Nun.
13.9: From the tribe of Binyamin: Palti, son of Raphu.
13.10: From the tribe of Zeḇulun: Gaddi’ĕl, son of Soḏi.
13.11: From the tribe of Yosĕph, from the tribe of Menashsheh: Gaddi, son of Susi.
13.12: From the tribe of Dan: Ammi’ĕl, son of Gemalli.
13.13: From the tribe of Ashĕr: Shĕthur, son of Miḵa’ĕl.
13.14: From the tribe of Naphtali: Naḥbi, son of Wophsi.
13.15: From the tribe of Gaḏ: Geu’ĕl, son of Maḵi.
13.16: These are the names of the men whom Mosheh sent to spy out the land. And Mosheh called Hoshĕa the son of Nun, Yahoshua.
13.17: And Mosheh sent them to spy out the land of Kena’an, and said to them, “Go up here into the Negeḇ, and go up to the mountains,
13.18: and see what the land is like, and the people who dwell in it, whether strong or weak, whether few or many,
13.19: and whether the land they dwell in is good or evil, whether the cities they inhabit are in camps or strongholds,
13.20: and whether the land is rich or poor, and whether there are forests there or not. And you shall be strong, and bring some of the fruit of the land.” Now the time was the season of the first-fruits of grapes.
13.21: So they went up and spied out the land from the Wilderness of Tsin as far as Reḥoḇ, near the entrance of Ḥamath.
13.22: And they went up through the Negeḇ and came to Ḥeḇron. And Aḥiman, Shĕshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anaq, were there. Now Ḥeḇron had been built seven years before Tso’an in Mitsrayim.
13.23: And they came to the wadi Eshkol, and cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes. And they bore it between two of them on a pole, also of the pomegranates and of the figs.
13.24: That place was called the wadi Eshkol, because of the cluster which the men of Yisra’ĕl cut down from there.
13.25: And they returned from spying out the land after forty days.
13.26: And they went and came to Mosheh and Aharon and all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl in the Wilderness of Paran, at Qaḏĕsh. And they brought back word to them and to all the congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
13.27: And they reported to him, and said, “We went to the land where you sent us. And truly, it flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
13.28: “But the people who dwell in the land are strong, and the cities are walled, very great. And we saw the descendants of Anaq there too.
13.29: “The Amalĕqites dwell in the land of the Negeḇ, while the Ḥittites and the Yeḇusites and the Amorites dwell in the mountains. And the Kena’anites dwell by the sea and along the banks of the Yardĕn.”
13.30: And Kalĕḇ silenced the people before Mosheh, and said, “Let us go up at once and take possession, for we are certainly able to overcome it.”
13.31: But the men who had gone up with him said, “We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we.”
13.32: And they gave the children of Yisra’ĕl an evil report of the land which they had spied out, saying, “The land through which we have gone as spies is a land eating up its inhabitants, and all the people whom we saw in it are men of great size.
13.33: “And we saw there the Nephilim, sons of Anaq, of the Nephilim. And we were like grasshoppers in our own eyes, and so we were in their eyes.”

14.1: Then all the congregation lifted up their voices and cried, and the people wept that night.
14.2: And all the children of Yisra’ĕl grumbled against Mosheh and against Aharon, and all the congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Mitsrayim! Or if only we had died in this wilderness!
14.3: “And why is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 bringing us to this land to fall by the sword, that our wives and children should become a prey? Would it not be better for us to turn back to Mitsrayim?”
14.4: And they said to each other, “Let us appoint a leader, and let us turn back to Mitsrayim.”
14.5: Then Mosheh and Aharon fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
14.6: And Yahoshua son of Nun, and Kalĕḇ son of Yephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their garments,
14.7: and they spoke to all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, “The land we passed through to spy out is an exceedingly good land.
14.8: “If 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has delighted in us, then He shall bring us into this land and give it to us, ‘a land which is flowing with milk and honey.’
14.9: “Only, do not rebel against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, nor fear the people of the land, for they are our bread. Their defense has turned away from them, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with us. Do not fear them.”
14.10: But all the congregation said to stone them with stones. Then the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared in the Tent of Appointment before all the children of Yisra’ĕl.
14.11: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “How long shall I be scorned by these people? And how long shall I not be trusted by them, with all the signs which I have done in their midst?
14.12: “Let Me smite them with the pestilence and disinherit them, and make of you a nation greater and mightier than they.”
14.13: And Mosheh said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Then the Mitsrites shall hear it, for by Your power You brought these people up from their midst,
14.14: and they shall say to the inhabitants of this land they have heard that You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are in the midst of these people, that You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are seen eye to eye and that Your cloud stands above them, and You go before them in a column of cloud by day and in a column of fire by night.
14.15: “Now if You shall kill these people as one man, then the nations which have heard of Your report shall speak, saying,
14.16: ‘Because 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 was not able to bring this people to the land which He swore to give them, therefore He killed them in the wilderness.’
14.17: “And now, I pray, let the power of Aḏonai be great, as You have spoken, saying,
14.18: ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is patient and of great kindness, forgiving wickedness and transgression, but by no means leaving unpunished; visiting the wickedness of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation.’
14.19: “Please forgive the wickedness of this people, according to the greatness of Your kindness, as You have forgiven this people, from Mitsrayim even until now.”
14.20: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said, “I shall forgive, according to your word,
14.21: but truly, as I live and all the earth is filled with the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
14.22: for none of these men who have seen My esteem and the signs which I did in Mitsrayim and in the wilderness, and have tried Me now these ten times, and have disobeyed My voice,
14.23: shall see the land of which I swore to their fathers, nor any of those who scorned Me see it.
14.24: “But My servant Kalĕḇ, because he has a different spirit in him and has followed Me completely, I shall bring into the land where he went, and his seed shall inherit it.
14.25: “Since the Amalĕqites and the Kena’anites are dwelling in the valley, turn back tomorrow and depart into the wilderness by the Way of the Sea of Reeds.”
14.26: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, and to Aharon, saying,
14.27: “How long shall this evil congregation have this grumbling against Me? I have heard the grumblings which the children of Yisra’ĕl are grumbling against Me.
14.28: “Say to them, ‘As I live,’ declares 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, ‘as you have spoken in My hearing, so I do to you:
14.29: ‘The carcasses of you who have grumbled against Me are going to fall in this wilderness, all of you who were registered, according to your entire number, from twenty years old and above.
14.30: ‘None of you except Kalĕḇ son of Yephunneh, and Yahoshua son of Nun, shall enter the land which I swore I would make you dwell in.
14.31: ‘But your little ones, whom you said would become a prey, I shall bring in, and they shall know the land which you have rejected.
14.32: ‘But as for you, your carcasses are going to fall in this wilderness.
14.33: ‘And your sons shall be wanderers in the wilderness forty years, and shall bear your whorings, until your carcasses are consumed in the wilderness.
14.34: ‘According to the number of the days in which you spied out the land, forty days - a day for a year, a day for a year - you are to bear your wickednesses forty years, and you shall know My breaking off.
14.35: ‘I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I have spoken, I shall do this to all this evil congregation who are meeting against Me: In this wilderness they are consumed, and there they die.’ ”
14.36: And the men whom Mosheh sent to spy out the land, who returned and made all the congregation grumble against him by bringing an evil report of the land,
14.37: even those men who brought the evil report about the land, died by the plague before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
14.38: Of those men who went to spy out the land, only Yahoshua son of Nun, and Kalĕḇ son of Yephunneh remained alive.
14.39: And when Mosheh spoke these words to all the children of Yisra’ĕl, the people mourned greatly.
14.40: And they rose up early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “See, we have indeed sinned, but we shall go up to the place which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had spoken of!”
14.41: But Mosheh said, “Why do you now transgress the command of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, since it does not prosper?
14.42: “Do not go up, lest you be smitten by your enemies, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is not in your midst.
14.43: “Because the Amalĕqites and the Kena’anites are there before you, and you shall fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is not with you.”
14.44: But they presumed to go up to the mountaintop, but neither the ark of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 nor Mosheh left the camp.
14.45: So the Amalĕqites and the Kena’anites who dwelt in that mountain came down and smote them, and beat them down, even to Ḥormah.

15.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
15.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When you have come into the land of your dwellings, which I am giving you,
15.3: and you make an offering by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, a burnt offering or a slaughtering, to accomplish a vow or as a voluntary offering or in your Appointed Times, to make a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, from the herd or the flock,
15.4: then he who brings near his offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall bring near a grain offering of one-tenth part of fine flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of oil,
15.5: and one-fourth of a hin of wine as a drink offering you prepare with the burnt offering or the slaughtering, for each lamb.
15.6: ‘Or for a ram you prepare as a grain offering two-tenth parts of fine flour mixed with one-third of a hin of oil,
15.7: and as a drink offering you bring one-third of a hin of wine as a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.8: ‘And when you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering, or as a slaughtering to accomplish a vow, or as a peace offering to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄,
15.9: then shall be brought with the young bull a grain offering of three-tenth parts of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil,
15.10: and bring as the drink offering half a hin of wine as an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.11: ‘This is what is done for each young bull, for each ram, or for each lamb or young goat.
15.12: ‘According to the number that you prepare, so you do for each one according to their number.
15.13: ‘Let all who are native do so with them, in bringing near an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.14: ‘And when a stranger sojourns with you, or whoever is among you throughout your generations, and would make an offering made by fire, a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, as you do, so he does.
15.15: ‘One Law is for you of the assembly and for the stranger who sojourns with you - a Law forever throughout your generations. As you are, so is the stranger before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.16: ‘One Torah and one Right-Ruling is for you and for the stranger who sojourns with you.’ ”
15.17: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
15.18: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land to which I bring you,
15.19: then it shall be, when you eat of the bread of the land, that you present a contribution to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
15.20: ‘Present a cake of the first of your dough as a contribution - as a contribution of the threshing-floor you present it.
15.21: ‘Of the first of your dough you are to give to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 a contribution throughout your generations.
15.22: ‘And when you sin by mistake, and do not do all these Commands which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spoken to Mosheh,
15.23: all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has commanded you by the hand of Mosheh, from the day 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gave command and onward throughout your generations,
15.24: then it shall be, if it is done by mistake, without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall prepare one young bull as a burnt offering, as a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, with its grain offering and its drink offering, according to the Right-Ruling, and one male goat as a sin offering.
15.25: ‘Then the kohĕn shall make atonement for all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and it shall be forgiven them, for it was by mistake. And they shall bring their offering, an offering made by fire to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and their sin offering before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, for their mistake.
15.26: ‘And it shall be forgiven all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl and the stranger who sojourns in their midst, because all the people did it by mistake.
15.27: ‘And if a being sins by mistake, then he shall bring a female goat a year old as a sin offering.
15.28: ‘And the kohĕn shall make atonement for the being who strays by mistake, when he sins by mistake before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to make atonement for him, and it shall be forgiven him.
15.29: ‘For him who makes a mistake there is one Torah, both for him who is native among the children of Yisra’ĕl and for the stranger who sojourns in their midst.
15.30: ‘But the being who acts defiantly, whether he is native or a stranger, he reviles 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and that being shall be cut off from among his people.
15.31: ‘Because he has despised the Word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and has broken His Command, that being shall certainly be cut off, his wickedness is upon him.’ ”
15.32: And while the children of Yisra’ĕl were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Shabbath day.
15.33: And those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Mosheh and to Aharon, and to all the congregation.
15.34: And they put him in under guard, because it had not been declared what should be done to him.
15.35: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “The man shall certainly be put to death, all the congregation stoning him with stones outside the camp.”
15.36: And all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh, and he died.
15.37: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
15.38: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and you shall say to them to make tsitsit on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a blue cord in the tsitsit of the corners.
15.39: “And it shall be to you for a tsitsit, and you shall see it, and shall remember all the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and shall do them, and not search after your own heart and your own eyes after which you went whoring,
15.40: so that you remember, and shall do all My Commands, and be qodesh unto your Elohim.
15.41: “I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim, who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, to be your Elohim. I am 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim.”

16.1: And Qoraḥ, son of Yitshar, son of Qehath, son of Lĕwi, took both Dathan and Aḇiram the sons of Eliyaḇ, and On, son of Peleth, sons of Re’uḇĕn,
16.2: and they rose up before Mosheh with some of the children of Yisra’ĕl, two hundred and fifty leaders of the congregation, called ones of the meeting, men of name.
16.3: And they assembled against Mosheh and against Aharon, and said to them, “Enough of you! For all the congregation is qodesh, all of them, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is in their midst. Why then do you lift up yourselves above the assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?”
16.4: And when Mosheh heard, he fell on his face,
16.5: and spoke to Qoraḥ and all his company, saying, “Tomorrow morning 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall make known who is His and who is qodesh, and come near to Him. And let Him bring near to Him the one whom He chooses.
16.6: “Do this: Take fire holders, Qoraḥ and all your company,
16.7: and put fire in them and put incense in them before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 tomorrow. And it shall be that the one whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 chooses is the qadosh one. Enough of you, sons of Lĕwi!”
16.8: And Mosheh said to Qoraḥ, “Hear now, you sons of Lĕwi:
16.9: “Is it little to you that the Elohim of Yisra’ĕl has separated you from the congregation of Yisra’ĕl, to bring you near to Himself, to perform the service of the Mishkan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and to stand before the congregation to serve them,
16.10: and that He has brought you near to Himself, you and all your brothers, the sons of Lĕwi, with you? Yet you seek the kehunnah as well?
16.11: “Therefore you and all your company are assembled against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And Aharon, what is he that you grumble against him?”
16.12: And Mosheh sent to call Dathan and Aḇiram the sons of Eliyaḇ, but they said, “We are not coming up!
16.13: “Is it little that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, that you would also seize total rule over us?
16.14: “Also, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us inheritance of fields and vineyards. Would you bore out the eyes of these men? We are not coming up!”
16.15: And Mosheh became very displeased, and said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Do not respect their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them, nor have I done harm to any of them.”
16.16: Then Mosheh said to Qoraḥ, “Tomorrow, you and all your company shall be there before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, you and they and Aharon.
16.17: “And take each one his fire holder, and you shall put incense in it. And let each one bring his fire holder before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, two hundred and fifty fire holders, and you and Aharon, each one with his fire holder.”
16.18: So each one took his fire holder, and put fire in it, and laid incense on it, and stood at the door of the Tent of Appointment with Mosheh and Aharon.
16.19: And Qoraḥ assembled all the congregation against them at the door of the Tent of Appointment. Then the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to all the congregation.
16.20: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, and to Aharon, saying,
16.21: “Separate yourselves from the midst of this congregation, and let Me consume them in a moment.”
16.22: But they fell on their faces, and said, “O Ĕl, Elohim of the spirits of all flesh! When one man sins, are You wroth with all the congregation?”
16.23: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
16.24: “Speak to the congregation, saying, ‘Move away from around the tents of Qoraḥ, Dathan, and Aḇiram.’ ”
16.25: So Mosheh rose up and went to Dathan and Aḇiram, and the elders of Yisra’ĕl followed him.
16.26: And he spoke to the congregation, saying, “Please turn away from the tents of these wicked men! Do not touch whatever belongs to them, lest you be consumed in all their sins.”
16.27: Then they moved away from around the tents of Qoraḥ, Dathan, and Aḇiram. And Dathan and Aḇiram came out and stood at the door of their tents, with their wives, and their sons, and their little children.
16.28: And Mosheh said, “By this you know that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has sent me to do all these works, not because of my own heart.
16.29: “If these die as all men do, or if they are visited as all men are visited, then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not sent me.
16.30: “But if 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 creates what is unheard of, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them up with all that belongs to them, and they go down alive into the grave, then you shall know that these men have scorned 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
16.31: And it came to be, as he ended speaking all these words, that the ground under them split apart,
16.32: and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households and all the men with Qoraḥ, with all their goods.
16.33: So they and all those with them went down alive into the grave, and the earth closed over them, and they perished from the midst of the assembly.
16.34: And all Yisra’ĕl who were round about them fled at their cry, for they said, “Lest the earth swallow us up!”
16.35: And a fire came out from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were offering incense.
16.36: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
16.37: “Say to El’azar, son of Aharon the kohĕn, to pick up the fire holders out of the blaze, for they are qodesh, and scatter the fire some distance away.
16.38: “The fire holders of these men who sinned against their own lives, let them be made into beaten plates as a covering for the altar. Because they brought them before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, therefore they are qodesh. And let them become a sign to the children of Yisra’ĕl.”
16.39: And El’azar the kohĕn took the bronze fire holders, which those who were burned up had brought, and they were beaten out as a covering on the altar -
16.40: a remembrance to the children of Yisra’ĕl that no stranger who is not of the seed of Aharon, should come near to offer incense before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and not be like Qoraḥ and his company - as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had said to him through Mosheh.
16.41: But all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl grumbled against Mosheh and against Aharon on the next day, saying, “You, you have killed the people of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.”
16.42: And it came to be, when the congregation assembled against Mosheh and against Aharon, that they turned toward the Tent of Appointment. And see, the cloud covered it, and the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared.
16.43: And Mosheh and Aharon came before the Tent of Appointment.
16.44: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
16.45: “Arise from amidst this congregation, and let Me consume them in a moment.” And they fell on their faces.
16.46: So Mosheh said to Aharon, “Take the fire holder and put fire in it from the altar, and lay incense on, and go, hurry to the congregation and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the plague has begun.”
16.47: And Aharon took it as Mosheh commanded, and ran into the midst of the assembly, and saw that the plague had begun among the people. And he laid on the incense and made atonement for the people,
16.48: and stood between the dead and the living. And the plague was stopped.
16.49: And those who died in the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died on account of Qoraḥ.
16.50: Then Aharon returned to Mosheh at the door of the Tent of Appointment, for the plague had stopped.

17.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
17.2: “Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and take from them a rod from each father’s house, all their leaders according to their fathers’ houses, twelve rods. Write each one’s name on his rod,
17.3: and write Aharon’s name on the rod of Lĕwi, for there is one rod for the head of each father’s house.
17.4: “You shall then place them in the Tent of Appointment before the Witness, where I meet with you.
17.5: “And it shall be that the rod of the man whom I choose buds, and I shall rid Myself of the grumblings of the children of Yisra’ĕl, which they grumble against you.”
17.6: And Mosheh spoke to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and all their leaders gave him a rod each, for each leader according to their fathers’ houses, twelve rods. And the rod of Aharon was among their rods.
17.7: So Mosheh placed the rods before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in the Tent of the Witness.
17.8: And it came to be on the next day that Mosheh went into the Tent of the Witness and saw that the rod of Aharon, of the house of Lĕwi, had budded, and brought forth buds, and blossomed and bore ripe almonds.
17.9: And Mosheh brought out all the rods from before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to all the children of Yisra’ĕl. And they looked, and each man took his rod.
17.10: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “Bring Aharon’s rod back before the Witness, to be kept as a sign against the rebels, so that you put an end to their grumblings against Me, lest they die.”
17.11: And Mosheh did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had commanded him, so he did.
17.12: And the children of Yisra’ĕl spoke to Mosheh, saying, “See, we shall die, we shall perish, we shall all perish!
17.13: “Anyone who comes near the Mishkan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 dies. Shall we be consumed - to die?”

18.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Aharon, “You and your sons and your father’s house with you are to bear the wickedness against the Miqdash, and you and your sons with you are to bear the wickedness against your kehunnah.
18.2: “But bring with you your brothers of the tribe of Lĕwi too, the tribe of your father to join you and serve you while you and your sons are with you before the Tent of the Witness.
18.3: “And they shall guard your charge, and the duty of all the Tent, but they do not come near the furnishings of the qodesh place and the altar, lest they die, both they and you.
18.4: “And they shall be joined with you and guard the duty to the Tent of Appointment, for all the service of the Tent, but a stranger does not come near you.
18.5: “And you shall guard the duty of the qodesh place and the duty of the altar, so that there be no more wrath on the children of Yisra’ĕl.
18.6: “And see, I Myself have taken your brothers the Lĕwites from the midst of the children of Yisra’ĕl - a gift to you, given by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to do the service of the Tent of Appointment.
18.7: “But you and your sons with you are to guard your kehunnah for all matters at the altar and behind the veil, and you shall serve. I have given you the kehunnah as a gift for service, but the stranger who comes near is put to death.”
18.8: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Aharon, “And see, I Myself have also given you the charge of My contributions, all the qodesh gifts of the children of Yisra’ĕl. I have given them to you for the anointing, and to your sons, as a Law forever.
18.9: “This is yours of the most qodesh gifts, from the fire: all their offerings, all their grain offerings and all their sin offerings and all their guilt offerings which they render to Me, are most qodesh for you and your sons.
18.10: “Eat it in the most qodesh place - every male eats it. It is qodesh to you.
18.11: “This also is yours: the contribution of their gift, with all the wave offerings of the children of Yisra’ĕl. I have given them to you, and your sons and daughters with you, as a Law forever. Everyone who is clean in your house eats it.
18.12: “All the best of the oil, and all the best of the new wine and the grain - their first-fruits which they give to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 - I have given them to you.
18.13: “The first-fruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, are yours. Everyone who is clean in your house eats it.
18.14: “All that is dedicated in Yisra’ĕl is yours.
18.15: “Everyone opening a womb of all flesh, which they bring to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, whether man or beast, is yours. But the first-born of man you shall certainly ransom, and the first-born of the unclean beast you ransom.
18.16: “And ransom their ransomed ones when one month old, according to your valuation, five sheqels of silver, according to the sheqel of the qodesh place, which is twenty gĕrahs.
18.17: “But the first-born of a cow, or the first-born of a sheep, or the first-born of a goat you do not ransom, they are qodesh. Sprinkle their blood on the altar, and burn their fat as an offering made by fire for a sweet fragrance to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
18.18: “And their flesh is yours, as the wave breast and as the right thigh, it is yours.
18.19: “All the contributions of the qodesh gifts, which the children of Yisra’ĕl present to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I have given to you and your sons and daughters with you as a Law forever. It is a covenant of salt forever before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with you and your seed with you.”
18.20: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Aharon, “You are not to have an inheritance in their land, nor have any portion in their midst. I am your portion and your inheritance among the children of Yisra’ĕl.
18.21: “And see, I have given the children of Lĕwi all the tithes in Yisra’ĕl as an inheritance in return for the service which they are serving, the service of the Tent of Appointment.
18.22: “And let the children of Yisra’ĕl no more come near the Tent of Appointment, lest they bear sin and die,
18.23: because the Lĕwites shall do the service of the Tent of Appointment, so they themselves bear their wickedness. A Law forever, throughout your generations: that among the children of Yisra’ĕl they are to have no inheritance,
18.24: but the tithes of the children of Yisra’ĕl, which they present as a contribution to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, I have given to the Lĕwites as an inheritance. That is why I have said to them, ‘Among the children of Yisra’ĕl they have no inheritance.’ ”
18.25: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
18.26: “Speak to the Lĕwites and say to them, ‘When you take from the children of Yisra’ĕl the tithes which I have given you from them as your inheritance, then you shall present a contribution of it to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, a tenth of the tithe.
18.27: ‘And your contribution shall be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing-floor and as filling from the winepress.
18.28: ‘Thus you also present a contribution unto 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 from all your tithes which you receive from the children of Yisra’ĕl. And you shall give from it the contribution to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to Aharon the kohĕn.
18.29: ‘From all your gifts you present every contribution due to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, from all the best of them, the qodesh part of them.’
18.30: “And you shall say to them, ‘When you have presented the best of it, then the rest shall be reckoned to the Lĕwites as the yield of the threshing-floor and as the yield of the winepress.
18.31: ‘And you shall eat it in any place, you and your households, for it is your reward for your service in the Tent of Appointment,
18.32: and bear no sin because of it, when you have presented the best of it, and do not profane the qodesh gifts of the children of Yisra’ĕl, lest you die.’ ”

19.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying,
19.2: “This is a law of the Torah which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has commanded, saying, ‘Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, that they bring you a red heifer, a perfect one, in which there is no blemish and on which a yoke has never come.
19.3: ‘And you shall give it to El’azar the kohĕn, and he shall bring it outside the camp, and shall slaughter it before him.
19.4: ‘And El’azar the kohĕn shall take some of its blood with his finger, and sprinkle some of its blood seven times toward the front of the Tent of Appointment.
19.5: ‘And the heifer shall be burned before his eyes - he burns its hide, and its flesh, and its blood, and its dung.
19.6: ‘And the kohĕn shall take cedar wood and hyssop and scarlet, and throw them into the midst of the fire burning the heifer.
19.7: ‘The kohĕn shall then wash his garments, and shall bathe his body in water, and afterward come into the camp, but the kohĕn is unclean until evening.
19.8: ‘And he who is burning it washes his garments in water, and shall bathe his body in water, and is unclean until evening.
19.9: ‘And a clean man shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and shall place them outside the camp in a clean place. And they shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl for the water for uncleanness, it is for cleansing from sin.
19.10: ‘And he who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his garments, and is unclean until evening. And it shall be a Law forever to the children of Yisra’ĕl and to the stranger who sojourns in their midst.
19.11: ‘He who touches the dead of any human being is unclean for seven days.
19.12: ‘He is to cleanse himself with the water on the third day, and on the seventh day he is clean. But if he does not cleanse himself on the third day, then on the seventh day he is not clean.
19.13: ‘Anyone who touches the dead of a human being, and does not cleanse himself, defiles the Mishkan of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. And that being shall be cut off from Yisra’ĕl. He is unclean, for the water for uncleanness was not sprinkled on him, his uncleanness is still upon him.
19.14: ‘This is the Torah when a man dies in a tent: All who come into the tent and all who are in the tent are unclean for seven days,
19.15: and every open vessel which has no cover fastened on it, is unclean.
19.16: ‘Anyone in the open field who touches someone slain by a sword or who has died, or a bone of a man, or a grave, is unclean for seven days.
19.17: ‘And for the unclean being they shall take some of the ashes of the heifer burnt for cleansing from sin, and running water shall be put on them in a vessel.
19.18: ‘And a clean man shall take hyssop and dip it in the water, and shall sprinkle it on the tent, and on all the vessels, and on the beings who were there, or on the one who touched a bone, or the slain, or the dead, or a grave.
19.19: ‘And the clean one shall sprinkle the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day. And on the seventh day he shall cleanse himself, and shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and shall be clean in the evening.
19.20: ‘But the man who is unclean and does not cleanse himself, that being shall be cut off from among the assembly, because he has defiled the Miqdash of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 - water for uncleanness has not been sprinkled on him, he is unclean.
19.21: ‘And it shall be a Law for them forever. And the one who sprinkles the water for uncleanness washes his garments. And the one who touches the water for uncleanness is unclean until evening.
19.22: ‘And whatever the unclean being touches is unclean. And the being who touches it is unclean until evening.’ ”

2.1: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying,
2.2: “The children of Yisra’ĕl are to camp, each one by his own banner, beside the sign of his father’s house. Let them camp around the Tent of Appointment at a distance.”
2.3: And on the east side, towards sunrise: those of the banner of the camp of Yahuḏah camp according to their divisions. And the leader of the children of Yahuḏah: Naḥshon, son of Amminaḏaḇ.
2.4: And his army with their registered ones: seventy-four thousand six hundred.
2.5: And those camping next to him is the tribe of Yissasḵar, and the leader of the children of Yissasḵar: Nethan’ĕl, son of Tsu’ar.
2.6: And his army with its registered ones: fifty-four thousand four hundred.
2.7: Then the tribe of Zeḇulun, and the leader of the children of Zeḇulun: Eliyaḇ, son of Ḥĕlon.
2.8: And his army with its registered ones: fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
2.9: All the registered ones of the camp of Yahuḏah, according to their divisions: one hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred. These depart first.
2.10: On the south side: the banner of the camp of Re’uḇĕn according to their divisions, and the leader of the children of Re’uḇĕn: Elitsur, son of Sheḏĕy’ur.
2.11: And his army with its registered ones: forty-six thousand five hundred.
2.12: And those who camp next to him: the tribe of Shim’on, and the leader of the children of Shim’on: Shelumi’ĕl, son of Tsurishaddai.
2.13: And his army with their registered ones: fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
2.14: Then the tribe of Gaḏ, and the leader of the children of Gaḏ: Elyasaph, son of Re’uw’ĕl.
2.15: And his army with their registered ones: forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
2.16: All the registered ones of the camp of Re’uḇĕn, according to their divisions: one hundred and fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty. And they are the second to depart.
2.17: And the Tent of Appointment, the camp of the Lĕwites, shall move out in the middle of the camps. As they camp, so they move out, everyone in his place, by their banners.
2.18: On the west side: the banner of the camp of Ephrayim according to their divisions, and the leader of the children of Ephrayim: Elishama, son of Ammihuḏ.
2.19: And his army with their registered ones: forty thousand five hundred.
2.20: And next to him the tribe of Menashsheh, and the leader of the children of Menashsheh: Gamli’ĕl, son of Peḏahtsur.
2.21: And his army with their registered ones: thirty-two thousand two hundred.
2.22: Then the tribe of Binyamin, and the leader of the children of Binyamin: Aḇiḏan, son of Giḏ’oni.
2.23: And his army with their registered ones: thirty-five thousand four hundred.
2.24: All the registered ones of the camp of Ephrayim, according to their divisions: one hundred and eight thousand one hundred. And they are the third to depart.
2.25: On the north side: the banner of the camp of Dan, according to their divisions, and the leader of the children of Dan: Aḥi’ezer, son of Ammishaddai.
2.26: And his army with their registered ones: sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
2.27: And those who camp next to him: the tribe of Ashĕr, and the leader of the children of Ashĕr: Paḡ’i’ĕl, son of Oḵran.
2.28: And his army with their registered ones: forty-one thousand five hundred.
2.29: Then the tribe of Naphtali, and the leader of the children of Naphtali: Aḥira, son of Ĕynan.
2.30: And his army with their registered ones: fifty-three thousand four hundred.
2.31: All the registered ones of the camp of Dan: one hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They depart last, with their banners.
2.32: These were registered ones of the children of Yisra’ĕl by their fathers’ houses. All who were registered according to their divisions of the camps: six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
2.33: But the Lĕwites were not registered among the children of Yisra’ĕl, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh.
2.34: And the children of Yisra’ĕl did according to all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded Mosheh. So they camped by their banners and so they departed, each one by his clan, according to their fathers’ houses.

20.1: And the children of Yisra’ĕl, all the congregation, came into the Wilderness of Tsin in the first month, and the people stayed in Qaḏĕsh. And Miryam died there and was buried there.
20.2: Now there was no water for the congregation and they assembled against Mosheh and against Aharon.
20.3: And the people contended with Mosheh and spoke, saying, “If only we had died when our brothers died before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!
20.4: “Why have you brought up the assembly of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 into this wilderness, that we and our livestock should die here?
20.5: “And why have you brought us up out of Mitsrayim, to bring us to this evil place? - not a place of grain or figs or vines or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink.”
20.6: Then Mosheh and Aharon went from the presence of the assembly to the door of the Tent of Appointment, and they fell on their faces. And the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 appeared to them.
20.7: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh, saying,
20.8: “Take the rod and assemble the congregation, you and your brother Aharon. And you shall speak to the rock before their eyes, and it shall give its water. And you shall bring water for them out of the rock and give drink to the congregation and their livestock.”
20.9: And Mosheh took the rod from before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 as He commanded him.
20.10: And Mosheh and Aharon assembled the assembly before the rock. And he said to them, “Hear now, you rebels, shall we bring water for you out of this rock?”
20.11: Then Mosheh lifted his hand and struck the rock twice with his rod. And much water came out, and the congregation and their livestock drank.
20.12: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, “Because you did not believe Me, to qadosh Me in the eyes of the children of Yisra’ĕl, therefore you do not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.”
20.13: These were the waters of Meriḇah, because the children of Yisra’ĕl contended with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and He was qadosh among them.
20.14: And Mosheh sent messengers from Qaḏĕsh to the meleḵ of Eḏom. “This is what your brother Yisra’ĕl said, ‘You know all the hardship that has befallen us,
20.15: that our fathers went down to Mitsrayim, and we dwelt in Mitsrayim a long time, and the Mitsrites did evil to us and our fathers.
20.16: ‘And we cried out to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and He heard our voice and sent the Messenger and brought us up out of Mitsrayim. And see, we are in Qaḏĕsh, a city on the edge of your border.
20.17: ‘Please let us pass over, through your land. We shall not pass over through fields or vineyards, nor drink water from wells, we shall go along the meleḵ’s highway. We shall not turn aside, right or left, until we have passed over your border.’ ”
20.18: But Eḏom said to him, “You do not pass over through me, lest I come out against you with the sword.”
20.19: And the children of Yisra’ĕl said to him, “We shall go by the highway, and if I or my livestock drink any of your water, then I shall pay for it. Let me only pass over on foot, without a word.”
20.20: But he said, “You do not pass over.” And Eḏom came out against them with many men and with a strong hand.
20.21: So when Eḏom refused to let Yisra’ĕl pass over through his border, Yisra’ĕl turned away from him.
20.22: And the children of Yisra’ĕl, all the company, departed from Qaḏĕsh and came to Mount Hor.
20.23: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon in Mount Hor near the border of the land of Eḏom, saying,
20.24: “Aharon is to be gathered to his people, for he is not to enter the land which I have given to the children of Yisra’ĕl, because you rebelled against My mouth at the water of Meriḇah.
20.25: “Take Aharon and El’azar his son, and bring them up to Mount Hor,
20.26: and strip Aharon of his garments and put them on El’azar his son, for Aharon is to be gathered to his people and die there.”
20.27: And Mosheh did as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 commanded, and they went up to Mount Hor before the eyes of all the congregation.
20.28: And Mosheh stripped Aharon of his garments and put them on El’azar his son. And Aharon died there on the top of the mountain. And Mosheh and El’azar came down from the mountain.
20.29: And when all the congregation saw that Aharon was dead, all the house of Yisra’ĕl wept for Aharon, thirty days.

21.1: And the meleḵ of Araḏ, the Kena’anite, who dwelt in the Negeḇ, heard that Yisra’ĕl was coming on the way to Atharim, and he fought against Yisra’ĕl and took some of them captive.
21.2: Then Yisra’ĕl made a vow to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and said, “If You deliver this people into my hand indeed, then I shall put their cities under the ban.”
21.3: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 listened to the voice of Yisra’ĕl and gave up the Kena’anites, and they put them and their cities under the ban. So the name of that place was called Ḥormah.
21.4: And they departed from Mount Hor by the way of the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Eḏom. But the being of the people grew impatient because of the way.
21.5: And the people spoke against Elohim and against Mosheh, “Why have you brought us up out of Mitsrayim to die in the wilderness? For there is no food and no water, and our being loathes this light bread.”
21.6: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people. And many of the people of Yisra’ĕl died.
21.7: Then the people came to Mosheh, and said, “We have sinned, for we have spoken against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and against you. Pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to take away the serpents from us.” So Mosheh prayed on behalf of the people.
21.8: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “Make a fiery serpent, and put it on a pole. And it shall be that everyone who is bitten, when he looks at it, shall live.”
21.9: So Mosheh made a bronze serpent, and put it on a pole. And it came to be, if a serpent had bitten anyone, when he looked at the bronze serpent, he lived.
21.10: And the children of Yisra’ĕl departed and camped in Oḇoth.
21.11: And they departed from Oḇoth and camped at Iyĕ ha’Aḇiram, in the wilderness which is east of Mo’aḇ, toward sunrise.
21.12: From there they departed and camped at the wadi Zereḏ.
21.13: From there they departed and camped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness that extends from the border of the Amorites, for the Arnon is the border of Mo’aḇ, between Mo’aḇ and the Amorites.
21.14: Therefore it is said in the Book of the Battles of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “Wahĕḇ in Suphah, the wadi Arnon,
21.15: and the slope of the wadi that turns aside to the dwelling of Ar, and lies on the border of Mo’aḇ.”
21.16: And from there on to Be’ĕr, which is the well where 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “Gather the people, and let Me give them water.”
21.17: Yisra’ĕl then sang this song: “Spring up, O well! Sing to it,
21.18: a well the leaders sank, which the nobles of the people dug by hacking with their staves.” Then from the wilderness on to Mattanah,
21.19: from Mattanah to Naḥali’ĕl, from Naḥali’ĕl to Bamoth,
21.20: and from Bamoth, in the valley that is in the country of Mo’aḇ, to the top of Pisgah which looks down on the wasteland.
21.21: And Yisra’ĕl sent messengers to Siḥon meleḵ of the Amorites, saying,
21.22: “Let me pass through your land. We shall not turn off into fields or vineyards, we shall not drink water from wells, but go by the meleḵ’s highway until we have passed over your border.”
21.23: But Siḥon would not allow Yisra’ĕl to pass through his border. So Siḥon gathered all his people together and went out against Yisra’ĕl in the wilderness, and he came to Yahats and fought against Yisra’ĕl.
21.24: And Yisra’ĕl smote him with the edge of the sword, and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Yabboq, as far as the children of Ammon, for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.
21.25: And Yisra’ĕl took all these cities, and Yisra’ĕl dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites - in Ḥeshbon and in all its villages,
21.26: for Ḥeshbon was the city of Siḥon the meleḵ of the Amorites, who had fought against the former meleḵ of Mo’aḇ, and had taken all his land from his hand as far as the Arnon.
21.27: That is why those who speak in proverbs say, “Come to Ḥeshbon, let the city of Siḥon be built and established.
21.28: “For fire went out from Ḥeshbon, a flame from the city of Siḥon. It consumed Ar of Mo’aḇ, the masters of the heights of the Arnon.
21.29: “Woe to you, Mo’aḇ! You have perished, O people of Kemosh! He has given his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity, to Siḥon the meleḵ of the Amorites.
21.30: “Then we shot them - Ḥeshbon has perished as far as Diḇon. And we laid waste as far as Nophaḥ, which reaches to Mĕyḏeḇa.”
21.31: So Yisra’ĕl dwelt in the land of the Amorites.
21.32: And Mosheh sent to spy out Ya’zĕr. And they took its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there,
21.33: and turned and went up by the way to Bashan. And Oḡ meleḵ of Bashan went out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Eḏre’i.
21.34: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, with all his people and his land. And you shall do to him as you did to Siḥon meleḵ of the Amorites, who dwelt at Ḥeshbon.”
21.35: And they smote him, and his sons, and all his people, until no remnant was left to him. And they took possession of his land.

22.1: And the children of Yisra’ĕl departed and camped in the desert plains of Mo’aḇ beyond the Yardĕn of Yeriḥo.
22.2: And Balaq son of Tsippor saw all that Yisra’ĕl had done to the Amorites.
22.3: And Mo’aḇ was exceedingly afraid of the people because they were many, and Mo’aḇ was in dread because of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
22.4: And Mo’aḇ said to the elders of Miḏyan, “Now this company is licking up all that is around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field.” Now Balaq son of Tsippor was meleḵ of the Mo’aḇites at that time,
22.5: and he sent messengers to Bil’am son of Be’or at Pethor, which is near the River in the land of the sons of his people, to call him, saying, “See, a people has come from Mitsrayim. See, they have covered the surface of the land, and are settling next to me!
22.6: “And now, please come at once, curse this people for me, for they are too strong for me. It might be that I smite them and drive them out of the land, for I know that he whom you baraḵ is baruḵ, and he whom you curse is cursed.”
22.7: And the elders of Mo’aḇ and the elders of Miḏyan left with divination fee in their hand, and they came to Bil’am and spoke the words of Balaq to him.
22.8: And he said to them, “Spend the night here, and I shall bring back word to you, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 speaks to me.” So the heads of Mo’aḇ stayed with Bil’am.
22.9: And Elohim came to Bil’am and said, “Who are these men with you?”
22.10: And Bil’am said to Elohim, “Balaq, son of Tsippor, meleḵ of Mo’aḇ, has sent to me, saying,
22.11: ‘See, a people has come out of Mitsrayim and cover the surface of the land. Come now, curse them for me. It might be that I am able to fight against them and drive them out.’ ”
22.12: And Elohim said to Bil’am, “Do not go with them. You do not curse the people, for they are baruḵ.”
22.13: And Bil’am rose in the morning and said to the heads of Balaq, “Go back to your land, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has refused to allow me to go with you.”
22.14: And the heads of Mo’aḇ arose and went to Balaq, and said, “Bil’am refuses to come with us.”
22.15: Then Balaq again sent heads, more numerous and more esteemed than they.
22.16: And they came to Bil’am and said to him, “This is what Balaq son of Tsippor said: ‘Do not be withheld from coming to me, please,
22.17: for I esteem you very greatly, and whatever you say to me, I do. Therefore please come, curse this people for me.’ ”
22.18: And Bil’am answered and said to the servants of Balaq, “Though Balaq were to give me his house filled with silver and gold, I am unable to go beyond the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 my Elohim, to do less or more.
22.19: “And now, please, you also stay here tonight, and let me find out what more 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 says to me.”
22.20: And Elohim came to Bil’am at night and said to him, “If the men come to call you, rise and go with them, but only the word which I speak to you that you do.”
22.21: And Bil’am rose in the morning and saddled his donkey, and went with the heads of Mo’aḇ.
22.22: But the displeasure of Elohim burned because he went, and the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 stationed Himself in the way as an adversary against him. And he was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
22.23: And the donkey saw the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 standing in the way with His drawn sword in His hand, and the donkey turned aside out of the way and went into the field. So Bil’am beat the donkey to turn her back onto the way.
22.24: Then the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 stood in a narrow passage between the vineyards, with a wall on this side and a wall on that side.
22.25: And when the donkey saw the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, she pushed herself against the wall and crushed Bil’am’s foot against the wall, so he beat her again.
22.26: And the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 went further, and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn aside, right or left.
22.27: And when the donkey saw the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, she lay down under Bil’am. So Bil’am’s displeasure burned, and he beat the donkey with his staff.
22.28: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Bil’am, “What have I done to you, that you have beaten me these three times?”
22.29: And Bil’am said to the donkey, “Because you have mocked me. If there were a sword in my hand, for I would have killed you by now!”
22.30: And the donkey said to Bil’am, “Am I not your donkey on which you have ridden, ever since I became yours, to this day? Was I ever known to do so to you?” And he said, “No.”
22.31: Then 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 opened Bil’am’s eyes, and he saw the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 standing in the way with His drawn sword in His hand. And he bowed his head and fell on his face.
22.32: And the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to him, “Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? See, I have come out to stand against you, because your way is reckless before Me.
22.33: “And the donkey saw Me and turned aside from Me these three times. If she had not turned aside from Me, I certainly would have killed you by now, and let her live.”
22.34: And Bil’am said to the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, “I have sinned, for I did not know You stood in the way against me. And now, if evil is in Your eyes, let me turn back.”
22.35: And the Messenger of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Bil’am, “Go with the men, but only the word that I speak to you, that you speak.” Bil’am then went with the heads of Balaq.
22.36: And when Balaq heard that Bil’am was coming, he went out to meet him at the city of Mo’aḇ, which is on the border at the Arnon, which was in the extremity of the border.
22.37: And Balaq said to Bil’am, “Did I not urgently send to you, calling for you? Why did you not come to me? Am I not able to esteem you?”
22.38: And Bil’am said to Balaq, “See, I have come to you! Now, am I at all able to say somewhat? The word that Elohim puts in my mouth, that I speak.”
22.39: And Bil’am went with Balaq, and they came to Qiryath Ḥutsoth.
22.40: And Balaq slaughtered cattle and sheep, and he sent some to Bil’am and to the heads who were with him.
22.41: And it came to be in the morning, that Balaq took Bil’am and brought him up to the high places of Ba’al, and from there he saw the extremity of the camp.

23.1: And Bil’am said to Balaq, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
23.2: And Balaq did as Bil’am had spoken, and Balaq and Bil’am offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
23.3: Bil’am then said to Balaq, “Stand by your burnt offering, and let me go on. It might be that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 comes to meet me, and whatever He shows me I shall declare to you.” And he went to a bare height.
23.4: And Elohim came to Bil’am, and he said to Him, “I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered on each altar a bull and a ram.”
23.5: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 put a word in the mouth of Bil’am, and said, “Return to Balaq, and this is what you say.”
23.6: And he returned to him and saw him standing by his burnt offering, he and all the heads of Mo’aḇ.
23.7: And he took up his proverb and said, “Balaq the meleḵ of Mo’aḇ has brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east. ‘Come, curse Ya’aqoḇ for me, and come, rage at Yisra’ĕl!’
23.8: “How do I curse whom Ĕl has not cursed? And how do I rage at whom 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not raged?
23.9: “For from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I observe him. Look, a people dwelling alone, not reckoning itself among the nations.
23.10: “Who shall count the dust of Ya’aqoḇ, and the number of one-fourth of Yisra’ĕl? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his!”
23.11: And Balaq said to Bil’am, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and look, you have continued to baraḵ!”
23.12: And he answered and said, “Should I not take heed to speak what 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has put in my mouth?”
23.13: And Balaq said to him, “Please come with me to another place from where you see them. You only see the extremity but not all of them. Curse them for me from there.”
23.14: And he took him to the field of Trophism, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
23.15: And he said to Balaq, “Stand here by your burnt offering while I meet over there.”
23.16: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 came to Bil’am, and put a word in his mouth, and said, “Go back to Balaq, and say this.”
23.17: So he went to him and saw him standing by his burnt offering, and the heads of Mo’aḇ with him. And Balaq asked him, “What did 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 say?”
23.18: And he took up his proverb and said, “Rise up, Balaq, and hear! Listen to me, son of Tsippor!
23.19: “Ĕl is not a man, to lie; nor a son of man, to repent! Has He said, and would He not do it; or spoken, and would not confirm it?
23.20: “See, I have received, to baraḵ. And He has baraḵ, and I do not reverse it.
23.21: “He has not looked upon wickedness in Ya’aqoḇ, nor has He seen trouble in Yisra’ĕl. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his Elohim is with him, and the shout of a Meleḵ is in him.
23.22: “Ĕl who brought them out of Mitsrayim, is for them like the horns of a wild ox.
23.23: “For there is no sorcery against Ya’aqoḇ, nor is there any divination against Yisra’ĕl. Now it is said to Ya’aqoḇ and to Yisra’ĕl, ‘What has Ĕl done!’
23.24: “Look, a people rises like a lioness, and lifts itself up like a lion; it lies not down until it devours the prey, and drinks the blood of the slain.”
23.25: And Balaq said to Bil’am, “Do not curse them at all, nor baraḵ them at all!”
23.26: And Bil’am answered and said to Balaq, “Have I not spoken to you, saying, ‘All that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 speaks, that I do’?”
23.27: And Balaq said to Bil’am, “Please come, let me take you to another place. It might be right in the eyes of Elohim that you curse them for me from there.”
23.28: And Balaq took Bil’am to the top of Pe’or, that overlooks the wasteland.
23.29: And Bil’am said to Balaq, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
23.30: And Balaq did as Bil’am had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

24.1: And when Bil’am saw that it pleased 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to baraḵ Yisra’ĕl, he did not go as at other times, to seek to use sorcery, but he put his face toward the wilderness.
24.2: And Bil’am lifted up his eyes and saw Yisra’ĕl encamped according to their tribes. And the Ruaḥ of Elohim came upon him.
24.3: And he took up his proverb and said, “The saying of Bil’am, son of Be’or, and the saying of the man whose eyes are opened,
24.4: the saying of him who hears the words of Ĕl, who sees the vision of Ĕl Shaddai, who falls down, with eyes opened wide:
24.5: “How good are your tents, O Ya’aqoḇ, your dwellings, O Yisra’ĕl!
24.6: “Like wadis that stretch out, like gardens by a river, like aloes planted by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, like cedars beside waters.
24.7: “He makes water flow from his buckets, and his seed is in many waters. His meleḵ is higher than Aḡaḡ, and his malḵuth is exalted.
24.8: “Ĕl who brought him out of Mitsrayim is for them like the horns of a wild ox; he devours nations, his enemies; and he breaks their bones, and he strikes through with his arrows.
24.9: “He bowed down, he lay down like a lion. And, like a lion, who would rouse him? Baruḵ is he who baraḵ you, and cursed is he who curses you.”
24.10: Then the displeasure of Balaq burned against Bil’am, and he struck his hands together. Balaq then said to Bil’am, “I summoned you to curse my enemies, and see, you have continued to baraḵ, these three times!
24.11: “And now flee to your place. I said I would greatly esteem you, and see, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has kept you back from esteem.”
24.12: And Bil’am said to Balaq, “Did I not also speak to your messengers whom you sent to me, saying,
24.13: ‘If Balaq should give me his house filled with silver and gold, I am unable to go beyond the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, to do either good or evil of my own heart. What 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 speaks, that I speak’?
24.14: “And now, see, I am going to my people. Come, let me advise you what this people is going to do to your people in the latter days.”
24.15: And he took up his proverb and said, “The saying of Bil’am, son of Be’or, and the saying of the man whose eyes are opened,
24.16: the saying of him who hears the words of Ĕl, and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of Ĕl Shaddai, who falls down, with eyes opened wide:
24.17: “I see Him, but not now; I observe Him, but not near. A Star shall come out of Ya’aqoḇ, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yisra’ĕl, and shall smite the corners of Mo’aḇ, and shall destroy all the sons of Shĕth.
24.18: “And Eḏom shall be a possession; and Sĕ’ir shall be a possession - enemies - and Yisra’ĕl is doing mightily.
24.19: “And a Ruler shall come from Ya’aqoḇ and destroy the remnant from Ar.”
24.20: He then looked on Amalĕq, and he took up his proverb and said, “Amalĕq was first among the nations, but his latter end is to perish forever.”
24.21: He then looked on the Qĕynites, and he took up his proverb and said, “Firm is your dwelling place, and your nest is placed in the rock,
24.22: but Qayin is to be burned. Till when does Ashshur keep you captive?”
24.23: And he took up his proverb and said, “Oh, who lives when Ĕl does this?
24.24: And ships shall come from the coast of Kittim, and they shall afflict Ashshur and afflict Ĕḇer, and so shall Amalĕq, and he also perishes.”
24.25: And Bil’am arose and left, and returned to his place. And Balaq also went his way.

25.1: And Yisra’ĕl dwelt in Shittim, and the people began to whore with the daughters of Mo’aḇ,
25.2: and they invited the people to the slaughterings of their mighty ones, and the people ate and bowed down to their mighty ones.
25.3: Thus Yisra’ĕl was joined to Ba’al Pe’or, and the displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 burned against Yisra’ĕl.
25.4: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Mosheh, “Take all the leaders of the people and hang them up before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, before the sun, so that the burning displeasure of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 turns away from Yisra’ĕl.”
25.5: And Mosheh said to the judges of Yisra’ĕl, “Each one of you slay his men who were joined to Ba’al Pe’or.”
25.6: And see, one of the children of Yisra’ĕl came and brought to his brothers a Miḏyanite woman before the eyes of Mosheh and before the eyes of all the congregation of the children of Yisra’ĕl, who were weeping at the door of the Tent of Appointment.
25.7: And when Pineḥas, son of El’azar, son of Aharon the kohĕn, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand,
